state.misconception_label: Does not understand that 2n represents an even number

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: Which of these shows part of the proof that the sum of two odd numbers is even? I got \( \begin{array}{l}2 n+(2 m+1) \\ =2(n+m)+1\end{array} \) because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: What if we break down the problem into simpler terms? Can you explain why you think \(2n+(2m+1) = 2(n+m)+1\) represents the sum of two odd numbers being even?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, well I thought 2n was odd and 2m+1 was odd, so I was adding them together? But now I'm not really sure... does 2n actually mean an odd number or something else? I'm confused about what the 2 in front means.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let me ask you this: what would happen if you tried your method on a simpler version of the problem?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, okay... so like, if I try 2n with actual numbers, if n is 3, then 2n would be 6, which is even, right? So 2n isn't odd at all - I think I got that backwards. But then I'm still confused about what 2m+1 means and how to show that two odd numbers add up to even?
